title: soft-fail-gatekeeper: region-aware shedder + tenant safety net
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an opt-in 'soft-fail gatekeeper' that attenuates hard circuit tripping by applying region-aware, tenant-scoped shedding and a temporary degraded response path. Feature-flagged; rollout via canary. No public API changes.
description:
Motivation: during recent regional pressure incidents we saw abrupt circuit flips that caused cascading hard-deny behavior for mid-tier tenants. This PR introduces a lightweight soft-fail gatekeeper inside the routing layer that applies gradual shedding (token-rate reduction + soft-deny responses) per-tenant and per-region before tripping a circuit. The goal is to preserve tail latency SLOs while avoiding wholesale tenant blackouts and large-scale reconnections.

Design summary: the gatekeeper implements a two-stage approach: (1) a fast region-aware estimator computes short-window load pressure and maps it to a shed score; (2) a tenant policy engine maps shed scores + tenant SLO priority to a soft action: prefix caching encouragement, reduced concurrency tokens, or a graceful 'degraded' response envelope (trimmed output, explicit 2xx-with-warning). Only when soft measures cannot stabilize does the existing circuit breaker engage. Key properties: hysteresis windows, exponential cool-down on reopen, k-v cache preservation hints, and telemetry anchors for post-incident analysis.

What changed (high level): added a new routing component (soft_gatekeeper) that hooks into request admission; expanded the tenant policy model to include 'soft_priority' and 'degrade_profile'; instrumented telemetry and traces for decision points; added feature flag + runtime config; tests and docs.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of region estimator and soft action engine
- [x] Unit tests for policy evaluation and hysteresis logic
- [x] Integration tests in benchmark-lab (canary) with simulated regional pressure
- [x] Observability: metrics + traces + dashboards added
- [x] Feature flag gated rollout config added to console
- [x] Rollback plan documented

Testing & validation: ran benchmark-lab scenarios (sustained 60% oversubscription for 3m, bursty 10x spikes) and measured a 3.1x reduction in tenant hard-trips and a 22% improvement in P99 tail latency under load compared to baseline. Integration canary in us-west-2 for 5% traffic ran for 48h with no regressions. All CI checks passed (lint, unit, integration).

Rollout plan: 1) Enable feature flag for 1% traffic in us-west-2 for 24h; verify metrics (slo.soft_fail.trigger_count, slo.circuit.opens) and latency P95/P99; 2) Increase to 10% if stable for 24h; 3) Global canary at 30% then full rollout. Canary opt-out available per-tenant via control-plane toggle.

Rollback & mitigations: the feature is behind a runtime feature flag and operator-safe toggle. If increased error rates are observed we will disable the flag and the system will revert to previous circuit behavior. A hotfix branch is prepared (hotfix/soft-fail-rollback) that reverts the gatekeeper wiring for targeted regions.

Related: SUP-1289 (tenant outages investigation), ENG-4523 (soft degrade design doc), ENG-4599 (policy model extension).

Notes: this change is intentionally conservative in default behavior (soft_priority defaults to 0). To avoid customer surprise the console shows an annotation when a tenant is affected by the gatekeeper and logs a human-readable reason with trace id for support flows.
